subject: Portability playbook + next tests (OpenAI-compat, hyperscaler gap)
messages:
From: Sean O'Neal <sean@cloudstride.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ellen Park <ellen.park@cloudstride.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick follow-up + data for portability discussion

Marcus — thanks again for the call this morning. High-level takeaways for us: we like Redwood's production focus (latency and rollout controls) but our procurement and infra teams want concrete evidence around:

- How close the OpenAI-compatible surface is (headers, SDKs, prompt/response diffs) — we run a fairly heavy prompt set with chained tool calls.
- Latency / cost deltas vs hyperscaler-managed endpoints when serving our typical 512 token median (plus worst-case spikes).
- What the SDK swap effort looks like (JS SDK + CI hooks) and any backward-compatibility gotchas.

I've attached a small evaluation matrix and a sample prompt set (partial) so you can scope the smoke tests. Can you flag the minimal tests that will give our architects confidence in a direct API/SDK swap? Also, we need a note on data residency (SLA/regional hosting) — are there constraints?

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30m next week once you propose a checklist.

—Sean
Cloudstride, Sr. Platform PM
[attachment: Cloudstride-eval-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sean O'Neal <sean@cloudstride.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 17:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + data for portability discussion

Sean — great to connect, and thanks for the matrix. I summarized the immediate, low-effort tests we suggest to demonstrate portability and to highlight where Redwood differs from hyperscalers:

1) OpenAI-compat smoke pass (owner: Marissa)
   - Run your canonical prompt set (provided) against the OpenAI-compatible endpoint on Redwood with identical request params.
   - Capture token-level outputs, top-k sampling seeds, and any structure differences (function-call payloads).
   - Deliverable: compatibility diff doc + failing prompt shortlist (1–2 days).

2) Hyperscaler baseline vs Redwood (owner: Ben)
   - 1-hour A/B with realistic concurrency for 512 token median; measure p50/p95/p99 latency, cost-per-1k tokens, and error modes.
   - Include quantized/FP16 runs if possible.
   - Deliverable: latency/cost delta table + short playbook for performance tuning (2–3 days).

3) SDK swap trial (owner: Ben + Marissa)
   - Integrate Redwood JS SDK into one of your non-critical microservices (feature-flagged).
   - Validate rollout, retry semantics, and CI smoke. Note SDK shim available to mirror OpenAI params.
   - Deliverable: integration notes + PR template for fast swap (2–4 days).

4) Data residency / SLA note (owner: Marcus)
   - We can provision region-specific endpoints (US-West, EU) for Dedicated/Private plans; hosted accounts can be pinned by region with appropriate contractual terms. I'll attach a short note on differences and a sample SLA.

Next steps: can you confirm the prompt set variant we should run (full vs sampled) and preferred window for the A/B run next Wed/Thu? I'll create a doc that maps each deliverable to acceptance criteria so your architects can sign off.

Attached: api-compat-diff.md (starter checklist). Linking a 30m slot: https://cal.example/marcus/30min

Best,
Marcus Lin
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
[attachment: api-compat-diff.md (text)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Portability playbook + next tests (OpenAI-compat, hyperscaler gap)

Looping in my quick runbook notes — high level:
- For the OpenAI-compat smoke pass: run with deterministic sampling (seeded) and record full response JSON. Focus on function_call payload differences first; many customers see structured-output mismatches there.
- For latency A/B: use our continuous-batching disabled to match hyperscaler single-request behavior, and then enable batching to show cost wins.
- SDK swap: prepare a small shim that maps 1:1 OpenAI param names to Redwood SDK (mostly headers + model param mapping). I’ll draft the shim and PR checklist today.

I'll start the smoke tests as soon as Sean confirms the sample size.

—Marissa
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Sean O'Neal <sean@cloudstride.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ellen Park <ellen.park@cloudstride.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:26:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Portability playbook + next tests (OpenAI-compat, hyperscaler gap)

Marcus / team — thanks, this is helpful. Quick answers:
- Run the sampled prompt set first (we've attached the 150-prompt subset we use for validation). If that looks good we'll expand to the full set.
- We can carve out a 2-hour window for the A/B test on Thu 19 Nov 15:00–17:00 PT (our infra team will stand by to throttle).
- Data residency: we prefer US-West-only for the pilot; we'll flag compliance constraints if the pilot passes.

I've uploaded the sampled prompts and the filled evaluation matrix. Let us know if you need additional headers or sample logs (we can redact).

—Sean
